head: A network for a million cars.
It got a few thousand.
slides.sub: How Better Place spent big on stations before it had drivers.

image.label: An empty battery-swap station glowing at night
image.brief: 밤의 이스라엘 고속도로 옆, 불이 켜졌지만 텅 빈 배터리 교환소. 차 한 대 없는 차선. 차갑고 쓸쓸한 영화 같은 톤. 로고 없음.

head: Electric cars had
one big fear.
body: In 2007, electric cars were expensive and ran out of power quickly. Drivers worried about getting stuck far from a charger.
Shai Agassi, a former SAP executive, founded Better Place with a bold answer: don't wait for better batteries. Swap them.

image.label: A silhouetted founder looking at a map of a small country
image.brief: 2000년대 후반 사무실, 작은 나라 지도를 바라보는 남성의 실루엣. 얼굴은 보이지 않게.

head: Buy the car.
Rent the battery.
body: Customers would buy a car without its battery. Better Place would own the batteries and sell driving like a phone plan, priced by distance.
On long trips, a robot would swap a dead battery for a full one in a few minutes, according to the company.

image.label: A robotic arm lifting a battery from under a car
image.brief: 차 아래에서 로봇 팔이 배터리를 꺼내는 장면. 깨끗한 산업 조명. 실제 차 디자인은 따라 하지 않음.

slides.label: raised from investors, by most reports
body: Investors bet that small countries like Israel and Denmark could go electric first. Renault agreed to build a car that worked with the swap stations.

image.label: A boardroom table with stacked funding documents
image.brief: 투자 계약서가 쌓인 회의실 탁자. 창밖으로 텔아비브 스카이라인. 인물 없음.

head: Lots of money, no drivers.
How do you launch?
body: You have one car model and no customers yet. Drivers won't buy until stations exist. Stations make no money without drivers.

options.text: Start with one city or a taxi fleet and grow from there
options.feedback: Slower and less dramatic. Investors expecting a national story might lose patience. Keep swiping.

options.text: Cover the whole country with stations and chargers before launch
options.feedback: Drivers would never feel stranded. But you pay for the full network before a single car sells. Keep swiping.

options.text: Wait until more carmakers sign on to use your batteries
options.feedback: More car choices would help. Waiting also burns cash and time. Keep swiping.

image.label: A map of Israel dotted with planned station pins
image.brief: 계획된 교환소 핀이 빼곡히 꽂힌 이스라엘 지도. 아직 비어 있는 도로.

head: The network came first.
The buyers didn't.
body: Better Place built dozens of swap stations and many charging spots across Israel before it sold cars there in 2012.
Buyers had one choice: a Renault Fluence Z.E. Other carmakers never joined, so the stations served just one model.

image.label: A single sedan parked at a large, empty swap station
image.brief: 넓고 텅 빈 교환소에 세단 한 대만 서 있는 장면. 무채색 톤.

slides.label: cars sold in Israel and Denmark, by most reports
body: That was far below what the network was built for. Every empty station still cost money to build and run.

image.label: A sparse parking lot with a few electric cars
image.brief: 몇 대의 전기차만 드문드문 서 있는 넓은 주차장. 위에서 내려다본 구도.

head: Agassi left.
The money ran out.
body: In October 2012, Agassi stepped down as CEO. New leaders cut costs, but sales stayed small.
In May 2013, Better Place filed for liquidation in Israel. Drivers were left with cars and stations no one would run.

image.label: A closed station with a chain across the entrance
image.brief: 입구에 쇠사슬이 걸린 문 닫힌 교환소. 흐린 하늘.

head: It scaled the supply
before proving demand.
body: Better Place faced a chicken-and-egg problem: no drivers without stations, no stations without drivers. It solved it by building everything at once.
With one car model and few buyers, the fixed costs of a national network arrived years before the customers.

image.label: A chicken and an egg drawn as circuit lines
image.brief: 닭과 달걀을 회로 선으로 그린 단순한 그래픽. 어두운 배경.

head: Prove one corner works,
then build the rest.
body: A big network is only an asset once people use it. Before that, it's a bill.
**Try it today:** what is the smallest market where you can show customers pay, before you spend on full scale?

image.label: One lit charging spot on a dark street
image.brief: 어두운 거리에 불이 켜진 충전 자리 하나.

factChecks.note: Better Place 설립(2007년)과 창업자 Shai Agassi의 SAP 임원 경력은 당시 보도와 Brian Blum의 책 'Totaled'(2017)로 확인하세요.
투자 유치 총액은 자료마다 약 8억 5천만 달러에서 거의 10억 달러까지 다릅니다. 카드에는 "more than $850 million, by most reports"로 적었습니다. 원문 보도로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] TechCrunch는 '8억 달러 이상'으로 보도. 8억 5천만 달러는 이번 검색에서 미확인.
Renault Fluence Z.E.가 배터리 교환을 지원한 사실상 유일한 차종이었다는 점, 이스라엘 상업 출시(2012년 초)는 Renault·Better Place 발표와 당시 보도로 확인하세요.

이스라엘·덴마크 판매 대수는 자료마다 다릅니다(이스라엘 약 1,000대 안팎, 합계 1,500대 미만으로 보도). 카드에는 "fewer than 1,500"과 "by most reports"로 적었습니다. 확인 후 조정하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 이스라엘 판매 1,000대 미만 확인(JTA). 덴마크 수치는 미확인이지만 '합계 1,500대 미만'과 모순 없음.
Agassi의 CEO 퇴진(2012년 10월)과 이스라엘 법원 청산 신청(2013년 5월)은 Reuters, Haaretz 등 당시 보도로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2013년 5월 26일 무렵 청산 신청, Agassi 퇴진은 그보다 8개월 전 확인.
교환소 수는 "dozens"로, 교환 시간은 "a few minutes, according to the company"로만 적었습니다. 정확한 수치는 넣지 않았습니다.

sources.text: Blum, B. (2017). Totaled: The Billion-Dollar Crash of the Startup That Took on Big Auto, Big Oil and the World.
Chafkin, M. (2014). A Broken Place: The Spectacular Failure of the Startup That Was Going to Change the World. Fast Company.
Reuters and Haaretz coverage of Better Place's liquidation filing (May 2013)
St. Louis Jewish Light/JTA: Better Place files for bankruptcy in Israel (2013)
